cq_coverage.details: All competency questions are structurally and semantically answerable with the classes and properties present. CQ5 is now explicitly supported via Organization, Address, and Identifier modeling; CQ13 is supported via ValidationConstraint and reference number properties. No CQ is missing or only partially covered.

strengths: Deep class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure and business roles
Good use of owl:equivalentClass and restrictions for core constructs
Comprehensive annotation of classes and properties
weaknesses: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) for aggregate constraints (e.g., total calculations)
Disjointness could be extended to more domain classes (e.g., Price vs Tax, Segment subclasses)
No explicit temporal modeling (dates, periods) for invoice events

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain or range in future property extensions)
P7 (Inverse properties are mostly present, but future relations may lack them)
reasoner_risks: Hermit and Pellet are compatible; no OWL 2 datatype violations or problematic axioms detected

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add General Class Axioms (GCAs) to express aggregate constraints, e.g., sum of LineItem net prices plus tax equals InvoiceSummary total.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables logical validation and increases semantic expressiveness for automated checks.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Extend disjointness axioms to more classes, including Segment subclasses and Price vs Tax.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves reasoning and error detection, reducing ambiguity in class membership.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce temporal properties (e.g., invoiceDate, deliveryDate) using xsd:dateTime for compliance with EN 16931-1 and future temporal queries.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables time-based queries and increases future-proofing for process tracking.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model additional EDIFACT segment types (e.g., DTM for dates/times, MOA for monetary amounts) for finer-grained mapping.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enriches the ontology for broader EDIFACT coverage and interoperability.

suggestions_addressed: Annotations are now fully complete on all classes and properties (previously partial)
CQ5 and CQ13 fully covered via structural modeling
suggestions_ignored: No General Class Axioms (GCAs) added for aggregate constraints
Disjointness not extended beyond previous scope
improvement_tracking.notes: Coverage remains perfect and quality improved slightly due to annotation completion and CQ5 explicit support. However, major structural improvements (GCAs, temporal modeling, broader disjointness) were not implemented, limiting further progress.

summary: The ontology remains robust and fully answers all competency questions, with improved annotation completeness and explicit support for previously ambiguous queries. Quality is high, but further semantic depth and validation logic are needed for optimal business and regulatory interoperability. The next iteration should focus on GCAs, temporal modeling, and richer disjointness.
